content.hypothesis: Prioritizing inspection of open surfaces (countertops, shelves) before closed storage units (cabinets, drawers, fridge) reduces search steps for tomatoes compared to semantic-prior-first (fridge) or arbitrary spatial order.
content.realization_pattern: Open-surface-first traversal: prioritize receptacles that do not require an 'open' action (countertops, shelves) over those that do (cabinets, drawers, fridge).
content.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks requiring cooling a perishable food item (tomato) where the target is not visible at entry and multiple receptacle types are present.

content.hypothesis: For perishable food items in mixed-layout kitchens, prioritizing inspection of open surfaces (countertops/shelves) before closed high-probability containers (fridge) yields fewer total search steps than starting with the semantically most likely container.
content.realization_pattern: Open-surface-first scan: traverse all visible open surfaces (countertops, shelves) before any closed storage units (fridges, cabinets, drawers).
content.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks where the target is a perishable food item (e.g., tomato) and the room contains both high-probability semantic containers (fridge) and low-probability open surfaces (countertops), testing if checking open surfaces first outperforms direct fridge inspection.
